primary_driver: The U.S.-Iran war is widening through Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure, while Russian strikes on Kyiv resumed during active U.S.-Ukraine diplomacy.
primary_stabilizer: Active U.S.-Ukraine diplomatic contacts and the scheduled NATO Ukraine Defence Contact Group meeting preserve limited crisis-management channels.

headlines.title: Houthi strikes set fire to Saudi oil sites and wound 73
headlines.summary: Iran-backed Houthi attacks on Saudi cities, energy facilities and utilities materially widen the U.S.-Iran conflict beyond the immediate theater and raise the risk of Gulf-state entry or retaliation.

headlines.title: Russian ballistic missiles hit Kyiv as U.S. envoys leave
headlines.summary: Russia resumed missile attacks on Kyiv shortly after U.S. negotiators departed, demonstrating continued high-intensity combat despite renewed diplomatic efforts and prompting Polish military aviation activity.

headlines.title: Zelenskyy says U.S. envoys brought ideas to end Russia's war
headlines.summary: The reported exchange of potentially useful proposals provides a limited stabilizing channel, although it has not yet produced a ceasefire or restrained Russian operations.

headlines.title: Oil rises as risks of prolonged Middle East conflict heighten supply worries
headlines.summary: Higher oil prices and renewed risk premiums around the Strait of Hormuz show that military escalation is producing immediate global economic effects and increasing pressure on energy security.

headlines.title: NATO Secretary General attends Ukraine Defence Contact Group meeting
headlines.summary: The meeting signals continued allied military support and institutional coordination for Ukraine, reinforcing alliance cohesion while also sustaining the risk of protracted confrontation with Russia.

areas_to_watch.name: Saudi Arabia and Gulf energy infrastructure
areas_to_watch.why: Further Houthi or Iranian attacks on oil, gas, ports or utilities could trigger direct Saudi or broader Gulf military retaliation and disrupt global energy flows.

areas_to_watch.name: Strait of Hormuz and commercial shipping
areas_to_watch.why: Threats to shipping and exposed energy assets create a high-impact pathway from regional combat to global economic and military escalation.

areas_to_watch.name: U.S.-Iran escalation ladder
areas_to_watch.why: Additional U.S. strikes, Iranian attacks on American forces or shipping, or attacks on Gulf partners could end the current intermittent pattern and produce sustained regional war.

areas_to_watch.name: Ukraine-Russia front and NATO airspace
areas_to_watch.why: Missile attacks near or across NATO borders, combined with Ukrainian strikes on Russian infrastructure, could create pressure for direct alliance involvement.

areas_to_watch.name: U.S.-Ukraine-Russia diplomacy
areas_to_watch.why: Diplomatic contacts are active but fragile; continued Russian attacks during negotiations could discredit the process and close the remaining de-escalation channel.

methodology.note: Analytical early-warning index, not a probability forecast.
methodology.formula: Weighted average of ten 0–10 factor scores, multiplied by 10 and rounded.
